The Congress of $CAPITAL$: Keep the Empire Strong

The great powers of Europe joined together in $CAPITAL$ to negotiate the future of the Balkans. While there was much contention, ultimately it was decided that the Ottoman Empire needed to be kept strong, and any demands placed on it should not weaken its interests unduly. Few of the attendees were pleased, the Russians in particular, and even though the Congress favored the Ottomans it remains to be seen whether they will bow to European pressure and uphold the Congress's edict.
This is how it must be.
The Congress of $CAPITAL$: Stabilize the Balkans

The great powers of Europe joined together in $CAPITAL$ to negotiate the future of the Balkans, with delegates from the Ottoman Empire also in attendance. While there was much contention, ultimately it was decided that creating stability in the region was best even if it came at the expense of the Empire's power. The Russian delegates were pleased, but Ottoman delegates left in a rage. It remains to be seen whether they will bow before the Congress's demands.
The Demands of the Congress

Our delegates have returned from the Congress in $FROMCOUNTRY$ with mixed news: though the consensus reached was that $COUNTRY$ needed to be kept strong, they still placed numerous demands upon us that would see the political map of the Balkans rearranged. If we choose to defy the European edict, we could be facing wars from many fronts.
We will abide by their demands.
Never! $COUNTRY$ will not be ordered about!
The Demands of the Congress

Our delegates have returned from the Congress in $FROMCOUNTRY$ with disheartening news: despite considerable dissension among those attending, a consensus was reached that creating stability in the Balkans is more important that $COUNTRY_ADJ$ interests and sovereignty. The demands are humiliating, and will see us losing much of the Balkans if we agree. If we defy the Congress, however, we could be facing war from many fronts.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ Agrees to the Demands

$FROMCOUNTRY$ has sent word to the European powers that it will abide by the decrees of the Congress. This proves to the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ government they are serious about working with the rest of Europe to maintain stability.
Good to hear.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ Agrees to the Demands

$FROMCOUNTRY$ has sent word to the European powers that it will abide by the decrees of the Congress. This proves to the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ government they are serious about working with the rest of Europe to maintain stability, though it is clear they are angered by the results.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ Defies the Congress
$FROMCOUNTRY$ has decreed that it will not abide by the demands of the Congress. The Treaty, they say, is so much worthless paper, and they refuse to give up any of their sovereignty.
They will pay for this.
We have no desire to push this further.
Giving Up Cyprus
We are called upon to live up to our part of the bargain and give up Cyprus.
We will abide by our agreement.
Their help was worthless! Forget it!
The Cyprus Lease
$FROMCOUNTRY$ has agreed to live up to its part of the bargain and hand over Cyprus.
Excellent.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ Reneges
$FROMCOUNTRY$ has reneged on its deal to give up Cyprus. They claim our aid at the Congress wasn't worthwhile.
Then we shall take it whether they like it or not!
It's not worth fighting over.
The Bosnian Stewardship
The Congress has agreed to our demands regarding Bosnia. They are to be placed under $COUNTRY_ADJ$ control.
Excellent!
Never mind.
The Croatian Stewardship
The Congress has agreed to our demands regarding Croatia. They are to be placed under $COUNTRY_ADJ$ control.
$FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ Allies
$FROMCOUNTRY$ received a great deal of benefit from the recent Congress of great powers, and it was decided that $COUNTRY$ deserves great influence in $FROMCOUNTRY$ as compensation -- if we want it.
Absolutely.
We have no interest in influencing $FROMCOUNTRY$.

$FROMCOUNTRY$ received a great deal of benefit from the recent Congress of great powers, and it was decided that $COUNTRY$ deserves considerable influence in $FROMCOUNTRY$ as compensation -- if we want it.
Influence in $FROMCOUNTRY$

$FROMCOUNTRY$ received a great deal of benefit from the recent Congress of great powers, and it was decided that $COUNTRY$ deserves considerable some small influence in $FROMCOUNTRY$ as compensation -- if we want it.
Legacy of the Congress

$COUNTRY_ADJ$ delegates were sent to the recent Congress -- reasonable considering it was the fate of our country and the entire Balkans that was being decided, or so we thought. As it turns out, the great powers of Europe decided what was to become of $COUNTRY$ without our participation, and while we received some benefit it has come to us at a price.
So be it.
$COUNTRY_ADJ$ Coup?

There is unrest among $COUNTRY_ADJ$ officers in the military, enough that some of them are actively spreading dissension among the ranks. $COUNTRY$ would be better served, they say, if the army was in charge rather than the current leadership -- elected it may be, but according to them it has proven too ineffective. And it seems many of the men under their command agree.
This could mean trouble down the line.
The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Military Coup

$COUNTRY_ADJ$ army forces in $CAPITAL$ have made their way toward the government buildings -- not to protect the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ government as is their duty, but instead to oust our leaders and install themselves as $COUNTRY$'s new rulers. They claim that $COUNTRY$ is in a state of 'upheaval', and only the army can restore order.
The army shall rule $COUNTRY$ for now.
We will not stand for military rule in $COUNTRY$!

The Paris Foreign Missions Society has been actively spreading Catholicism in $COUNTRY$ for many years now, or perhaps we should say they are attempting to, as they have encountered considerable resistance among the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ people. Recently, in the southern region of Cochinchina, one of the local aristocrats took offense to the intrusion of several missionaries and executed them -- without our leave. Word of the deed has reached the attention of the French government, meaning their eye will almost certainly turn to us.
This does not bode well.
Persecution of French Missionaries

The Paris Foreign Missions Society has been actively spreading Catholicism in Asia for many years now, but they have encountered considerable persecution at the hands of Asian authorities. In $FROMCOUNTRY$, the execution of several missionaries in the Cochinchina region has prompted the society to ask the French government for diplomatic intervention. So far, discussion has gone nowhere and the idea has now arisen that forming a protectorate in the area may be our only solution.
Demand Cochinchina, or it is war.
We will continue on the diplomatic path.
The $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ Demand

First they send their 'missionaries' into our country, flouting our laws and offending our people with their spouted nonsense. They turn our own citizens away from the righteous path, and expect us to do nothing? $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ have seized upon this excuse to demand all of Cochinchina in recompense.
Turn over Cochinchina. There is nothing we can do.
They are a paper tiger. Let them come, if they dare.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ Has Refused
The rulers of $FROMCOUNTRY$ have foolishly refused our demands.
Then war it is.
The Suzerainty of Cambodia

We have an issue before us. The Vietnamese rule over our kingdom, and it seems certain that, very soon, either they or the Thai will demand we submit in full and are swallowed whole. The French stand on our borders, eyeing Indochina with their own ambitions. Perhaps they will make kinder rulers? Rebellion seems almost certain to end with Cambodia being torn to pieces by both.
Ask for Foreign protection.
Throw out the Thai! We will risk war.
The King of Cambodia

King Norodom of Cambodia has sent our government a request: he asks that the Foreigners intervene in his nation, demanding it be released from Vietnamese control and made our protectorate. This would suit our goals in Indochina, though it risks war.

Cambodia has been under Vietnamese control since our war with Siam. Now it seems the Cambodia king has approached the Foreigners and asked for protection, and the Foreigners have agreed to offer it. They are demanding control over Cambodia, on threat of war.
Demand Cambodia from the Vietnamese.
Cambodia is on its own.
Surrender Cambodia.
This cannot be permitted!
Dai Nam Has Refused
Dai Nam has refused to surrender Cambodia to us. It seems we have little choice but to act.
War it is.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ Has Refused
The $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ have refused to intervene. It seems we are on our own.
Then we declare our freedom. We shall risk war.
Then we do nothing.
$COUNTRY_ADJ$ Indochina
Many in our government believe we should press our influence in Indochina, expanding our colony there to include some of our less civilized neighbors. Perhaps the time is right for war?
It remains a possibility.
This is not in our interests.

The Construction of the Eiffel Tower

Work on the foundations of the Eiffel Tower began. Those for the east and south legs were straightforward, each leg resting on four 2 m (6.6 ft) concrete slabs, one for each of the principal girders of each leg but the other two, being closer to the river Seine, were more complicated: each slab needed two piles installed by using compressed-air caissons 15 m (49 ft) long and 6 m (20 ft) in diameter driven to a depth of 22 m (72 ft) to support the concrete slabs, which were 6 m (20 ft) thick. Each of these slabs supported a block built of limestone each with an inclined top to bear a supporting shoe for the ironwork. Each shoe was anchored into the stonework by a pair of bolts 10 cm (4 in) in diameter and 7.5 m (25 ft) long. The foundations were complete by $YEAR$ and the erection of the ironwork began. The main structural work was completed at the end of March 1889 and today Eiffel celebrated this by leading a group of government officials, accompanied by representatives of the press, to the top of the tower. Since the lifts were not yet in operation, the ascent was made by foot, and took over an hour, Eiffel frequently stopping to make explanations of various features. Most of the party chose to stop at the lower levels, but a few, including Nouguier, Compagnon, the President of the City Council and reporters from Le Figaro and Le Monde Illustré completed the climb. At 2:35 Eiffel hoisted a large French flag, to the accompaniment of a 25-gun salute fired from the lower level. There was still work to be done, particularly on the lifts and the fitting out of the facilities for visitors, and the tower was not opened to the public. A Papal Bull

The Papacy has reacted to the purging of the Latin quarter with expected outrage, declaring these actions to be ''ungodly'' and ''of equivalent barbarity to the very Yamagate the Hellene people were liberated from,'' and in turn has issued a Papal bull, excommunicating the church in the east for allowing these atrocities to occur. The Patriarch in Constantinople has in turn excommunicated the Pope, declaring the state of Rhomania to be wholly independent of Papal influence, and regarding this as a cynical attempt to utilize the actions of the secular state to grab more ecclesiastical power for Rome. It appears the actions of Eastern Rome on this day have festered a divide between the two churches, one that may well never be bridged again.
Justinians Ambition

Justinian, only recently coronated, has in front of him a great and terrible duty, that of reorganizing and restoring the legal apparatus of the old Byzantine Empire from the ground up. Chief amongst his great concerns is that of reorganizing the Senate, a body that stands as a useless remnant of Rome's far republican past. To be a Senator remains an unimportant prestige position, and in this modern age serves as naught but a hotbed for liberal agitation amongst the Rhomaion intelligentsia. Justinian, fashioning himself as a legal reformer like his saintly namesake, sees potential in empowering this body, particularly in regards to securing the empire against resolving future succession crises. Some aristocrats, however, warn that an empowered senate may well prove a dangerous body should it be handed legal power once again, and suggest instead dismantling this anachronism once and for all.
The Senatorial Conspiracy

Justinian's abysmal failure in keeping the Aromanian peoples from engaging in military action against the Empire has greatly sullied the political favor of him across the state. The Senate especially, partially empowered and largely staffed by liberal agitators as it is, has found his incompetence in statecraft vexing. With military support for his rule at an all time low, and political opposition to the government quickly rising, the Senate has enacted a coup and removed the Basileius from power, proclaiming itself a restoration of both Roman republicanism and Hellenic democracy. Onlt time will tell if this gamble will turn in the Senate's favor...
The Senate Backs the Emperor!

The recent rebellion at the hands of the Aromanian population of the empire has come at great surprise to the Senate and aristocracy of the empire, convinced wholly of the Emperor's competent and capable rule. The meaningless rebellion has been fully denounced by the Senate, and the government stands wholeheartedly behind the efforts of Justinian to put down the uprising.
The Emperor Remains Absolute!

Despite all evidence to the contrary, the empire remains firmly behind the Basileius and his efforts to put down the Aromanian traitors. One inadvertent result of his ultimate depowering of the Senate, however, is the rise of liberal agitation across the countryside. Those senators whom have seen their station reduced by the empire have begun to agitate in the countryside for reform, greatly damaging the emperor's reputation amongst the peasantry.
The Fate of the Rhomaion Empire

The Kachyskaya Kurdish peoples have, since the reconquest of Anatolia, been firmly under Rhomaion grasp as a subservient slave population. According to a new law passed by the central government, these peoples would be made free citizens within the nation as a whole. This motion has immediately caught the ire of not only the aristocracy, but most of the general population. The reaction to this unholy deed, as the popular representatives of the Hellenes call it, was the beginning of a series of riots that first destabilized, then eradicated the central governing authority of the Byzantine royal family. Now, the Emperor has fled, and the revolutionaries hold full control over what remains, proclaiming a new Hellenic Empire in its ashes.
The Eagle Burns

The reckoning for the atrocities wreaked upon the Latin peoples in Greece are at hand. The whole of the Eastern Empire burns now, its territories sacked and destroyed en masse, and the lands of the Balkans and Anatolia carved up by our victorious men into various duchies and fiefdoms. The withering Byzantines are left only with the lands of Thrace itself as a last holdout and remnant of their rule, propped up as a mere puppet regime charged to placate the locals and merely cement our rule. The East, once the glorious bastion of eastern Christendom, has fallen forevermore.
The Scouring of Rome

The planned triumph for the reconquest of Rome quickly devolved out of the control of Rhomaion authorities. The sight of the Pope, the father of the so-called Holy See to the barbaric 'Italian' peoples being whipped like the dog he was drove the plebeian populace of Rome to violence. For three days, Rhomaion military authorities lost control of the city streets, as riots and looting turned into revolutionary fervor against the reclaimers of Roman glory. However, as with the kingdoms and empires before them, they could not prevent military authority from reestablishing itself in the seat of Roman power. The streets were scoured, building by building, and punitive measures were taken to utterly decimate the population of the once-great city, which proceeded to run red with barbarian blood. The Rhomaion state has wisely followed this up, decreeing the end of Italic liberties across the Rhomaion empire, and the beginning of rightful settlement of the peninsula by their true masters from Constantinople. Such shall be the fate of all who defy our reconquest.
Rome shall be consecrated in blood.
The Scythian Question

The reconquest of old Anatolia complete, another question now plagues the Empire's halls in Constantinople: that of the Scythians in the north of Anatolia. Long ago, when the barbarians of the east first arose to tear these lands away from civilization, the Magyar Scythians invaded from the north in the chaos and seized much of the Trebizontine and Paphlagonian coast for themselves. Even now, these populations, with backing from a city-state enclave under northern Magyar protection, agitate against our rule. While these savages have no right to life within our lands, it may still prove slightly more viable to grant them some modicum of autonomy, administered from their petty city-state. Alternatively, we may simply destroy the city, and subjugate the masses as is.
They can have their petty autonomy.
These traitorous barbarians are worthy only of death.
The Scythian Reckoning

The city state proved more difficult to subjugate than planned, due to the support it enjoyed in the northern coast of Anatolia, their so-called 'homeland.' The barbarians still did not prove enough to halt the great armies of the Rhomaion Empire, and their petty settlements were ultimately overrun by the guns of Roman armies. The remnant populations are being exterminated in the aftermath of the war, and those few which we graciously leave behind shall be put to work in the Thracian countryside and our plantations.
These heathens shall infest the coastline no longer.
The Hungarian Theme Clandestinely Requests Annexation

The Del-Mogyr of northern Anatolia, long our separated brothers due to geography and political dissent over the future of the Hungarian nation, have requested our aid in breaking them out of Byzantine control. The faux empire has claimed lordship over them, and even now the Del-Mogyr feel the noose ever-tightening around their necks. We have a chance now to reunite our people, only with the perfidious Greeks to try and stop us.
We have our chance, and we must take it.
We're wimps and can't do it.
A Scythian League defies us!

The traitorous barbarians of the Del-Mogyr could never have been trusted with even the short leash we allowed for them. They have formed into a league with the treasonous Magyars of the Black Sea and demanded their independence from us under force of arms. Little do we care. We shall burn their people to the ground, and it shall be their women and children whom fear our wrath the most.
They shall burn.
Eventually! When we get around to it!
The Scouring of the Black Sea

The Magyar coalition has been felled at last. The Scythian barbarians, both north and south, have fallen to our blades and kneel before us, prostrated beneath their masters. Rome shall not be denied, and its vengeance shall be swift. Their fields are to be burned, their people are to be taken from their homes to work for their betters, and the world shall remember now and always the cost of dealing with Rome.
And so passes the Magyar into history.
The Cosenzan Coup

It is no secret that the Cosenzan League, the weakest amongst the Southern Italian States and the only republic of the confederal trio, only reluctantly joined the Confederation for fear of Carthaginian domination. Now, with Byzantine backing, the Cosenzans have pressed their hand, demanding a far-increased role in Southern Italian governance, and an effective abolition of monarchial power in the rest of Southern Italy. Soldiers loyal to Cosenza have marched on the capital in Melfi, attempting an open overthrow of the Confederation. Should they succeed, it is doubtless that Byzantium will only press further. Should they fail, it means war with Byzantium...and quite possibly with Cosenza as well.
Long live the Cosenzan Republic! Long live Italia!
Put these republican conspirators and Byzantine sycophants to the sword!
The Southern Italian Confederation Expels Byzantine Influence!

The Cosenzan hardliners failed in their task to seize total power over the Italian Confederation, and now the Italian government has ousted all Rhomaion influence in their affairs, and expelled the Rhomaion legation from their country. We now have little choice but to either lick our wounds and flee from Italian affairs forever, or to double down on our efforts and subjugate them by force. One piece of consolation remains, in that should we so choose to put them down by force, the Cosenzan hardliners will undoubtedly willingly separate themselves from the Confederation and aid our efforts.
To Melfis we will march!
Are you even Roman?
The Cost of Victory

We may have seized control of the Italian Confederation's government, but it is becoming increasingly apparent that we have not succeeded in our efforts. The Italian population increasingly regards the Cosenzan government as a vassalic regime under Byzantine domination, and this narrative is unfortunately anything but myth. It is Byzantine aid that sustains us, and it was Byzantine guns that put us in power. Now, we must either accept this reality and prostrate ourselves to them to save our languishing regime, or attempt now at this final hour to recover some legitimacy and expel the Byzantines...though this will not prevent those hardliners among our ranks from seceding and joining them.
We cannot survive without Constantinople.
We did not trade one monarchy for another!
The Cosenzans Request our Intervention

The Cosenzan government, as expected, cannot sustain itself as the legitimate government for all of Southern Italia. Now, as the government begins to suffer increasing instability in the face of public dissent, the Cosenzans request our support in putting down these uprisings and placing the region under a permanent Rhomaion protectorate. The ancient province of Longobardia returns to us finally, and we can return rightful Roman governance to these lands once again.
Send the governor.
The Conquest of Longobardia

The Italian Confederation, regardless of its efforts, failed to prevent the Rhomaion reconquest of their lands. Despite the desires of many hardliners among the Greek populations of the Empire, moderating Aromanian influences prevented the worst of their desired vengeance on the Italian people. The territory now falls back into Roman hands, and regional governors are being appointed for the new Themata Longobardia, bringing the ancient province back to the fold of its ancient forebears.
Send the governor.
The June War

Not since the Battle of the Adriatic has the Roman Empire come to blows with the usurpers in Carthage. After our fleets were destroyed and our foothold in Magna Graecia lost to the upstart duchy of Melfis, our interests once again turned away to the ever-volatile Anatolian frontier. Now, however, in our moment of greatest weakness, Carthage once again seeks to oust us from our recently acquired gains. Never again shall we suffer this loss!
Never again shall they take our glory!
Victory in the June War

The barbarian Greeks sought to bring their cruelty and malice to the lands of Holy Italia once again, to our ancient homelands, but we have cast them out. The Italians, who just a few years ago saw us as villains and adversaries, now welcome us as liberators, here to save them from the yoke of Constantinople. How the great saint of Rome would turn in his grave, if he were to see what had become of his works in the East.
More glory lies in our mercy than in their vanity.
Victory in the June War

At last, our terrible defeat in 1547 has been avenged! The supremacy of the Rhomaion people in Magna Graecia now stands uncontested by the heretics in Carthage. Finally, true civilization can return to these lands. Despite our greatest hopes, these lands cannot be fully administered in our diminished state. To alleviate concerns of overreach, and diminish the likelihood of a regional uprising, the Themata Longobardia shall be recreated, granting the locals some modicum of autonomy from the central government in Constantinople.
It will only be temporary.
The Fool's Crusade

The Aquileian Patriarch, a foolish ecclesiarch that was already in 'light' schism with Constantinople for centuries before now, has clearly decided after the limp-spined so-called Pope excommunicated us that it has an opportunity now to drive its heretical sword into the heart of the Church of Holy Athena. But no, it is not the hieresiarchs, bankrolled by Venetian merchants and controlled by the Semites, so accursed in the sights of Heaven, that shall determine the fate of the lands of Italia and Graecia. We shall burn their paltry ports to ash before we ever submit.
Their ''church'' will burn.
The Liberation Crusade

Mere excommunication was not enough to sate the bottomless greed of the heretics in Constantinople. Their cultish adherence to their petty nationalism, exclusionary to all Christians under God and tyrannical to all peaceful and kind peoples of the world, does not allow it. Excommunication, therefore, is not enough to cease their aggression. Now, the Papacy has but one choice left: to call a Crusade to liberate Italy once and for all.
In one year's time, Italy shall be freed in the name of God.
The real Crusade

The fool had allies. Or perhaps we were the fools, to think the Papacy, envious of our status as it was for all these years, would not escalate the conflict. The crusade they call for is not the paltry affair of the Aquileians, and already our grip is slipping over the lands we have already taken, as Italians flock to their banner. The war that is coming shall not be a simple endeavor, and indeed it seems all of the barbarians are joining to do away with us. §RThis war can only be won or lost. Victory shall secure the dream of Magna Graecia, and defeat shall bury it.
Our future hangs on the edge of the knife.
The Great Italian War

The Crusade, it seems, has finally borne fruit. Our governor-generals in Siculia, Aquileia, and Cosenza have all reported a complete loss of civil order, and our garrisons have been driven out from Italy almost altogether. The Papacy and their allies have seized upon the opportunity and declared war on us, vowing to 'free' Italy from its rightful overlords. §RThey will die where they stand.
Victory in the Crusade!

The Crusade has been successful, casting the barbaric Greeks from the lands of Italia. The damage done by these wars has been severe, and the many casualties elicited by this terrible war may never truly be recovered from, but now, with the Holy Church as the one true head of Italia, perhaps, just perhaps, this is the end of our tribulations.
Italia Subdued

The godless of Italia have been quelled at last. The last pieces of resistance, whether by soldier or clerk, man or woman, old or infantile, are in the process of being crushed. Our ancient glory returns to us, as the Angel Athena promised. A ceremony has been prepared to 'gift' the state the Western Imperial Regalia. Though it was long lost, there is little reason not to forge it anew, like our empire. After all, who is left to question our authority?
The Armenian Quagmire

The conquest of Armenia was thought to have passed by smoothly, and indeed for a short time it appeared as if the Armenians were grateful to have been subjugated by their rightful overlords. However, as the government sought to extract its rightful labor quotas and enforce religious and cultural compliance, the Armenians showed their true face. Withdrawing to mountainous settlements and refusing to acknowledge Rhomaion authority, the Armenians have entered into a state of rebellion against the Empire, one not easily crushed.
Damn those mountains!
End of the Caucasian Hell

The rebellion in the Caucasus has been quelled. The advent of modern industrial-logistical infrastructure allowed for the mass expansion of Rhomaion garrisons in the once-distant Armenian mountains, and modern firearms made previously effective rebel counterattacks less and less capable for lack of supply. The lands of Armenia and Georgia, now, have gone quiet. The Rhomaion state has moved to enact its revenge upon those who are left, and a great and terrible cry shall arise from the land.
Like has never been heard before or since.
The Reconquest of Antioch

The city of Antioch, one of the five seats of the ancient Pentarchy, has been restored to the Rhomaion Empire. The local, heretical patriarch has been ousted from his seat, to be replaced by a proper religious leader who understands the holy mission of the Angel. The locals are left unharrassed to an acceptable extent, after the proper, customary looting. The prophecy shall come to pass.
The holy mission marches on.
Reconquest of Syria-Palaestina

Jerusalem, the very same city whereupon the Rhomaion God gave his ministry of the sword to the perfidious, rebellious Semites, has finally been restored to Roman rule. In proper celebration, all signs of the prior, unholy squatters has been eliminated, and their bodies shall be piled underneath the site of a new, glorious temple to the Angel.
The Angel Athena commands, and we obey.
The Conquest of Alexandria

The ancient and glorious city of Alexandria, constructed by our great forebears even before the Gospel of Athena was revealed to them, has fallen once again into Rhomaion hands. The local savages are to be employed and put to use in restoring this lands' usefulness to us. They shall build great monuments and farm every iota of land across the Nile for every bit of its worth. Never again shall a Hellene starve while a barbarian lives!
The Angel smiles, for it is good.
Karchidóna propeí na katastrafe?

Carthage must be destroyed. So commands the prophecy, so commands Athena. So commands she in the name of the heavens above that the city be sacked and destroyed forevermore. Not a stone shall be unturned, not a babe within the womb left unmolested by our fury, not a man or woman nor infant shall be left alive in these forsaken lands. Carthage is no more. It shall never be again.
§RThrough tears of blood, the Angel smiles.
§RTHE PROPHECY FULFILLED

Through great lamentations, through the red waters of sacrifice to the skies above, the Angel Athena smiles upon us! The prophecy fomented in our darkest days when we were subjugated by the Anatolian infidels has been fulfilled! Forevermore shall the Angel guide us, forevermore shall the backs of all beneath us be broken beneath the eternal wheel of civilization and empire eternal. We raise our hands and hearts, clutching still at the throat of our enemies, in supplication to the divine powers that granted us this victory.
The Great Temple of Athena shall adorn Constantinople forevermore!
The City of Rome is restored to us! Praise be to Athena!
The Pella Mining Company

The advent of new forms of industry and resource extraction have proven of particular use to us in the lands of Anatolia. The lands of Central Anatolia are not particularly conducive to industrial, large-scale agriculture. What it is conducive to is mining. With our control over Kachuskayan labor complete, it is a quite simple transition, albeit with a body count. A new state corporation is being created to handle the transition, named after the ancient capital of the Macedonian Empire, another manifestation of our ancient glory.
Acceptable losses.
The Gospel of Athena

Published in 1798, the "Gospel of Athena" represents the formation of the modern Rhomaion identity. Published during the height of the Kachuskayan occupation in the Peloponnese, the conditions under which this religious-political tract were published were dire. A dire starvation had set in due to the occupation and the disruption of mercantile shipping, and the Kachuskayan occupation only worsened it through mass confiscation of foodstuffs to supply their war effort. The work itself details a prophecy from the Angel Athena to an onlooking Greek scribe in the year 117. She proclaims the decline of the great Rhomaion empire, the loss of many lands, and even the contemporary struggle against Kachuskaya. She follows with an admonition to service, proclaiming that the barbarians of the world "shall be swept away as Tyre and Babylon, to fall unto lamentations forevermore." The work represents the formulating ideal of Hellenic politics, wherein She proclaims the true meaning of the Star of David, that the points represent the hearts of Hellenic civilization, the rightful holdings of the Empire before peace shall be brought to the world, perfection where the Hellenes shall forevermore rule all things.
Carthage, Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, Jerusalem
The Hellenic Interregnum

It has been many centuries since the Hellenic people have known any governance other than the ancient institution of the Basileius or the Senate, barring the occupation from Kachuskaya. Even less accustomed to the changing times are those barbarians, so intolerable to the new regime, facing the real inevitability of their cleansing from the lands of the Hellenes. Indeed, with the chaos in the government, these nationalist uprisings may have a chance at victory...we must not let that happen.
We shall let nothing go.
The Despotate

The chaos in the streets was anathema to the Hellenic Council's interests. While lesser regimes may have flagged and failed in the face of such adversity, the council in Constantinople successfully restored public confidence in the regime through the rapid deployment of military personnel throughout Greece and Macedonia. Through blood and iron this new administration has cemented itself, and under these trying times, the Hellenic Council has formed a Despotate, a ruling executive body headed by Alexandros Argaed, a man from Thessalia who claims, in most likely apocryphal fashion, descent from the oldest and greatest leader of Hellenic history. A deeply competent and amibitious man, he will prove either a great boon to the Despotate or its undoing.
Alexandros shall lead us to glory!
The Fate of the Latins

The Hellenic council has not forgotten about the betrayal of the Latins. They were meant to defend their Hellenic superiors, not turn against them in the name of its enemies in the lands of the Kachuskayans. Traitors all of them, the Hellenic Council has decided they shall be done away with in a final manner. Not a single Latin shall be left alive when the affair is done.
These lands shall be Greek once again.
A Developing Cult of Personality

Alexandros has become increasingly popular amongst both civilian and party officials in the past months. His alleged bloodline meshes well with the increasing rejection of the old Rhomaion identity, now associated with a traitorous dynasty that sold away Hellene rights and supremacy for their own gain. The lineage of the Makedonas serves as a popular refutation of the old order, and some worry that his connections to the Makedons, alongside his popular appeal, may pose the threat of a renewed monarchy, contrary to the revolution's ideals.
Long live Alexandros!
The New Capital

The old capital of Constantinople, how accursed that name is now, has been found to bear too many connections to the old monarchy and its outdated political norms. The Hellenes must choose for themselves a new capital, a new place to call home not connected to the old order. The council has found that Thessalonike is the most promising candidate for such a new capital, and preparations have commenced to move the capital there. In the meanwhile, the old capital has been given a more fitting rename, based on the lesser city-state that it once comprised. The so-called Patriarch, too, has been banished from his former seat.
Fitting for the modern age of Hellenes.
The Hellenic Heartland

The Hellenic state's constitution, reaffirming the great powers of the Revolution, also have defined its borders. Within the borders of the Hellenic realm are all those lands that have historically been a part of the realms of Athena, tied to the Hellenes in perpetuity. The Hellenic state shall forevermore incorporate all of the lands of Thrace, Attica, the Peloponnese, Thessaly, Paphlagonia and Smyrna, Teebizond, Cappodocia, Cilicia, and all other realms within Anatolia, as well as the ancient frontier of the Caucasus and the Levant.
Glory be!
The Angel's Prophecy?

The destruction of the Rhomaion Empire, and by its own hands, no less, comprised a deadly blow to the belief in the angel's prophecy as it was. After all, if it was not to be the Rhomaions to whom the world were inherited, then what was the promise to be? The Hellene state, with no small effort, has found older copies of the prophecy that date far earlier than any recognized before. Here, it is revealed that it was never an angel at all, as the usurping Romans interpreted it, but rather the Goddess herself, the patron of the Hellenes. To them she promised not mere seats upon this earth, but the whole of all they ever set foot upon, lands that shall be made empty in her name for them to inhabit forevermore.
The Goddess leads us forevermore!
The Reconstruction of the Parthenon

To honor the Goddess Athena, first her temple must be reconstructed. First converted into a heretical church to the demon from Philistina that impersonated the Goddess, then later destroyed in part by the great hordes of Kachuskaya, the temple has long been desecrated by foreign rites and foreign customs, if not outright damaged. In the glory of the Hellenic people, Alexandros has placed his great faith in the reconstruction efforts, wagering both his wealth and his reputation on his ability to tie the efforts to his own personal glory. Regardless, the effort will take much time, and a great many resources, as the craftsmen's work is ill-suited for modern industrial machinery, and the marble remains exceedingly expensive.
Glory to the Goddess!
Reinauguration of the Parthenon

The Parthenon has, after so long being reconstructed, finally been completed! Inaugurated with new effigies of the goddess, purged of foreign influences and false gods, the temple is a true testiment to the glory of the Hellenic state and its people. Alexandros has personally overseen the dedication of the temple, and the implications of his oversight have become clear. The speech hardly spoke of the Parthenon at all, rather than his contributions to it, likening himself to the great Diadochi of old, and even to Alexander the Great. The party now faces the threat that he may yet ride this popularity into a new throne for himself. He has already claimed for himself the title of "Diadochite," claiming an elevated place amongst equals in the Revolution.
Long Live the Diadochite!
The Diadochite Coup

Alexandros has made his move. Amassing a large following of close associates, he deigned to make a march on Thessalonike, betting that his charisma and charm would muster the revolutionary guard to his aid. It is only a matter of if they disperse the rabble, or allow his ploy to succeed.
All Hail Alexandros!
An unfortunate end befalls the would-be king.
The Tsakonian Helots

The Diadochite coup awoke in the Hellene population a newfound sense of identity. Indeed, if one man could make such a bold march into the capital to make demands, could not any man end the Revolution at any moment? Or, could not the Hellene people, if properly militarized, perpetuate it in eternity? Many "Tsakonian" orders have emerged in the aftermath of the coup, proclaiming themselves as militant orders in the Spartan tradition, here to safeguard the interests of the Revolution now and forevermore. They pledge themselves to individual, militant firebrands who claim to be the sole representative of the Revolution, yet simultaneously pledge their undying allegiance to the ruling government.
Odd, but useful.
The Egyptian Famine

Cash crop shipments have been reducing month by month for the past year, and only now is it becoming apparent to the government why. Much of the river Nile itself has been reduced, silted and reseource-drained through the constant inundation of low-lying cash crops. Moreover, many plots of land have found that local fauna, particularly locusts and frogs, have taken to devouring the cash crops en masse. With the government continuing to force the production of these valuable cash crops, and local food production having long since crashed, the stage has been set for a terrible famine, one which it is unknown when or if it will end.
But what about my tobacco?
The Rending of Kachuskaya

The mountains run red with Kachuskayan blood. Men, women, children alike are lined one after the other, made to watch as family members are gunned down, or made to participate in the fell deed themselves. The industrial scale of this massacre has horrified all outside of the Hellenic world, but the only response Thessalonike shall offer them is one of the sword. Kachuskaya sought the end of the Hellenic world, and so too shall the Hellenes be the ones to slay the Kachuskayans forevermore.
Bleed them dry.
The end of Ashur

We are well aware what the ancient Assyrians did to our forebears, the true children of Athena in the promised land of the Levant. Many mounds of bodies are laid at the feet of the Assyrian barbarians, and now their people shall be brought to an end. The city of Ninevah has been leveled utterly, its citizens scattered, sent overseas as blind leading the blind. All who could be found have been mutilated, cut apart like the Hellenes they cut from the promised land. The lands of Athena shall be cleansed forevermore from their filth, no matter how much international agencies wail and bemoan this as the destruction of an ancient and proud civilization.
All the world revolves around Thessalonike.
The reconquest of Egypt

The lands of Alexander himself have been reclaimed by our efforts. Alexandria, the ancient and proud Hellenic city, now rests once again in Hellenic hands, and the barbaric foreigners that occupy what belonged to the Ptolemies shall now be expelled. Their fields shall be salted, their people sent in chains overseas or killed. The land of the Ptolemies shall be Hellenic, and only Hellenic, forevermore. No longer shall Pharoahs make dictates from ancient thrones that were never theirs, but now only the heirs to Alexander shall have their will be done as gods upon this earth.
Alexandria rests with Athena now.
The Scraping of Tyre

The lands of the Levant shall be scraped like a rock, swept into the ocean and drowned with their ancient kin who disobeyed the will of Athena. The descendants of the Philistines whom Theseus slew alongside Goliath shall be eradicated utterly. Jerusalem, where the ancient kingdom of Minos built the temple most high to Athena, in appeasement after his courting of the lesser god Poseidon, shall be reconsecrated in Her name. The Goddess of Wisdom and Maiden-lord of Heaven shall smile upon our deeds, when these ancient lands of Hellas are restored unto it.
...do you follow? I dont.
The Revenge of Mithridates

The great king Mithridates, last among the Hellenes to oppose the encroachment of the Latins of Rome, once had his great kingdom encompass the whole of the Caucasus and the Baltic Sea. His ancient empire is once again in our hands, and now the many steppe hordes and foreigners, chief among them the Caucasian "natives" and the Hungarians, shall be expelled in their entirety, replaced now with Tsakonian homesteads and military settlements.
Pontus shall be Greek again.
The Seleucid Inheritance

The lands of the first great Parsi dynasty, the Seleucids, once again fall into the hands of the Goddess. Athena proclaimed many years ago that Persia would once again be populated solely by the Hellenic peoples, and that the ancient enemies of the Goddess from the lands of the devil Mani would be purged utterly. Now, the ancient Greek civilization is being freed from the vermin that infest it, and the inheritance of the Seleucids and their founder in Dionysus shall be claimed in the Goddess' name once again.
what
The Furthest Frontiers

The furthest frontiers Hellenic civilization ever encompassed now fall within the hands of Thessalonike. These lands, even to the current administration, were never truly fully encompassed by Hellenic peoples, but rather the semi-civilized Scythians. With modern technology, however, and the blessing of the Goddess, this shall change. New homesteads shall be created to populate these barren steppes, never populated by any but a few savages, with Hellene settlers. Whatever few mongrels exist in these lands shall be purged, and nobody will care.
Resettling the east almost makes you wish for a Scythian winter.
The Angel of Death

The first colony was named Noa Lilibbeu, after his hometown. After his incredible discovery, the Emperor of the Romans, Micheal IX Vandu, bestowed upon him the title of Exarch and Governor of "Amazzogna" (Named after an encounter between Andronicus and a tribe where it was custom that also women fought as soldiers). Altough officially the name of the colony was Amazzogna, the European colonists started calling it Selbapunnica, for the type of wood that populated the coast of the land. In Afri-Romanni, Selba means forest and Punnicu is the color of the deep red dye that those trees produced.
The natives

The policy of castration was controversial in the nation, many calling it unhumane, but most lords inforced it anyway. This caused the slave population to plummet, so the colonist began bringing Berber slaves from Mauria or Nundia. The Emperor also struck a deal with the King of Kongo, creating a massive slave trade, that is secretly and illegally still around today...
The Andronic dynasty

Initially the first Exarch of Amazzonia was from a family of merchants, but Andronicus asked the Emperor to make the title hereditary, The Emperor agreed, as Andronicus was an expert in trading and was also popular with the colonials in Amazzogna. As his family was elevated to nobility, the Iovianic dynasty began marrying Carthaginian royalty, cementing it's newly aquired position even more, becoming a pseudo cadet branch of the Vandu dynasty.
The birth of a culture

The colonists from Carthage quickly adapted to the new territories, building houses, roads, churches and town halls. Andronicus helped forming the first provinces of his exarchate, declaring the capital to be Noa Lilibbeu, but later on the more rich city of Irriu de Bennarzu would become the capital. The culture of the Afri-Romanni population would mix with the local and slave population, forming a Selbapunnic way of life. The northern part of the nation would have a more war-like culture, with the constant attacks from Frankish colonists and soldiers in the many wars that were fought between eachother. For some time northern Selbapunnica would be controlled by Francia, but the revolts were continuous. Eventually they sedated the revolts but Carthage reconquered the territories in a colonial war. The dialects of the north find more germanic loanwords, while the southern ones find more native american loanwords.
A peaceful independence

As the Revolutionary wars in Europe ended, the idea of liberty and self-determination caught the population of the new world, making independence from their masters of the old continent a new strive of their lives. The Exarchate of Amazzogna was now to big to control, and the Emperor of Carthage knew that. Following a major reform in the Empire, with the biggest one being the abolishion of slavery, in 1818 the Emperor decided to give freedom to the Exarchate, before ensuring a truce of atleast 50 years and a short timed alliance to make the newly independent nation a close ally. The Constitution of Hanover

When King William died, Princess Victoria became Queen of the United Kingdom. Ernest Augustus became the King of Hanover. Many Hanoverians were of a liberal perspective, and would have preferred the popular viceroy, the Duke of Cambridge, to become king, but both of Ernest's younger brothers refused to lend themselves to any movement by which they would become king rather than their elder brother. Hanover had received its first constitution, granted by the Prince Regent, in 1819. This did little more than denote Hanover's change from an electorate to a kingdom, granted by the Congress of Vienna. The Duke of Cambridge, as King William's viceroy in Hanover, recommended a thorough reorganisation of the Hanoverian government. William IV had given his consent to a new constitution in 1833. The Duke of Cumberland's consent was neither asked nor received, and he had formally protested against the constitution's adoption without his consent.
The Göttinger Seven Protest

About one month after he succeeded to the throne, King Ernest addressed the matter of the Constitution. He stated that he was not bound by it, as his consent had not been asked to it. He also indicated that it would have been different, or perhaps even non-existent, had he been in power at the time of its composition. He declared that it was his aim and ambition to make the necessary changes to the constitution and rewrite it to reflect his values. Hearing this, Friedrich Christoph Dahlmann - a famous german historian -, made an attempt to persuade his colleagues at the University of Göttingen senate to disapprove of the king's intent to change the constitution, and take some form of action. At first, none of his colleagues were willing to support him. But when King Ernest annulled the constitution, Dahlmann again appealed to the university, and composed a protestation in regards to opposing Augustus' decision. This time, he received a better response, six other professors were now willing to sign as opposers. These six, plus Dahlmann, would become known as the Göttingen Seven.
The Göttinger Seven

Immediately upon his arrival in Hanover, the new King Ernest August dissolved the parliament which had been convened under the disputed constitution. He proclaimed the suspension of the constitution, on the ground that his consent had not been asked, and that it did not meet the kingdom's needs. The King issued a patent, declaring the constitution void, but upholding all laws passed under it. The 1819 constitution was restored. In carrying the King's patent into effect, the Cabinet required all officeholders (including professors at Göttingen University) to renew their oaths of allegiance to the King. Seven professors (including the two Brothers Grimm) refused to take the oaths, and agitated for others to protest against the King's decree. Since they did not take the oaths, the seven lost their positions, and the King expelled the three most responsible (including Jacob Grimm) from Hanover. However, he was widely criticised in other parts of Germany and Europe.

Vormärz

In 1836, the states of the German Confederation were in the middle of the so-called 'Vormärz' (pre-March). The name derived from the later (failed) revolution in the march of 1848, and was a period which was shaped by the Austrian and Prussian police states, the censorship of the press and restricted freedoms. But it was also the time of german romanticism, evolving nationalism and great personalities, which made germany to the land of poets and thinkers. German culture blossomed, intellectuals stood up against reactionary governments, and such ideas as national unity and wider suffrage became topics of a new liberal and democratic movement.
The kneeling controversy

Traditionally, Bavaria was a catholic state. But with the foundation of the kingdom and the annexations of surrounding lands in the Napoleonic age, Bavaria gained large territories which were protestant. In this time, the king promoted a more tolerant politic toward his subjects. An example was the edict, that protestant soldiers had not to knee in front of a catholic mass or procession. However, Minister Karl von Abel has proposed to change this.
The Blittersdorf Era

Baden was one of the most liberal states in the German Confederation. However, in the late 1830s and beginning 1840s, minister Friedrich von Blittersdorf went against the liberal and democratic traditions of Baden. He promoted monarchic traditions, which lead to much discontent among the liberal society of this south german country. Deutsches Wörterbuch

Das Deutsche Wörterbuch (The German Dictionary) is one of the most important dictionaries of the German language. It is for German what the Oxford English Dictionary is for English, containing detailed historical information about the origin and use over time of German words, with examples taken from actual documents. In German the dictionary is also known as 'Der Grimm'. It was started by the Grimm brothers (known also for Grimms' Fairy Tales) in 1838.  Initially the Grimm brothers expected the project to take ten years and produce 6–7 volumes. In fact, the first volume was not published until 1854. Wilhelm Grimm died in 1859, and Jacob in 1863, while working on the entry for 'Frucht' (fruit). After their deaths multiple institutions were involved in the work, including the Prussian Academy of Sciences and the Berlin Academy, with a center in Goettingen also involved. Finally completed in 1961, the dictionary will contain 32 volumes and include about 350,000 main entries. The 'Grimm' was not only a scientific, but also national work.
Deutschland. Ein Wintermärchen

In 1843, the german poet Heinrich Heine, who left Germany 1831 for France, went back for a few weeks, visiting his mother and publisher Julius Campe in Hamburg. Heine was not a typical romantic author, but more a satirical one who criticized the reactionary policy and censorship of the authoritarian german states, but also his nationalistic and chauvinistic compatriots. On the return journey to Paris, the first draft of 'Deutschland. Ein Wintermärchen' (Germany: A Winter's Tale) took shape. The verse epic appeared in 1844 published by Hoffmann and Campe, Hamburg. According to the censorship regulations of the Carlsbad Conference of 1819, manuscripts of more than twenty folios did not fall under the scrutiny of the censor. Therefore it was published together with other poems in a volume called ‘New Poems’. The work showed Heine’s world of images and his folk-song-like poetic diction in a compact gathering, with cutting, ironic criticisms of the circumstances in his homeland. Heine’s verse-epic was much debated in Germany.

Still always that wooden pedantic race/ Still always a right angle/ In every movement and every face/ The frozen conceit.' Heine, a former Prussian citizen (he was born in Düsseldorf), was against the militarism in his own country. Goethe Monument

The citizens of Frankfurt have edified a monument to honour Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, perhaps the most important german-speaking author and a symbol of german culture in general. This event is regarded as a national sensation among liberals and patriots.
The Constitutional Conflict

Like Baden, Hesse-Kassel had a rather liberal constitution. Humboldt's Kosmos

Kosmos (usually referred to in English as 'Cosmos') was an influential treatise on science and nature written by the German scientist and explorer Alexander von Humboldt. Kosmos began as a lecture series delivered by Humboldt at the University of Berlin, and was published in five volumes between 1845 and 1862 (the fifth was posthumous and incomplete). Widely read by academics and laymen alike, it applied the ancient Greek view of the orderliness of the cosmos (the universe) to the Earth, suggesting that universal laws applied as well to the apparent chaos of the terrestrial world. Controversially for the time, Humboldt in Kosmos spoke of the spirituality of the natural world only in general terms, avoiding the notion of a creator.
Robert Schumann

Robert Schumann is regarded as one of the most representative composers of the Romantic era. In 1850, he suceeded Ferdinand Hiller as musical director and moved to Düsseldorf. Although criticized regarding his poor conductor skills and scoffed because of his 'creative decay', Schumann composed his last symphony, the 'Rhenish'. He used Beethoven's and Mendelssohn's symphonies as a model, but was also inspired by his impressions of the Rhineland. Schumann himself stated, that his journey to Cologne and the sight of the cathedral were his main inspiration for this composition, which became one of his most famous works.
Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy

Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy was a German composer, pianist, organist and conductor of the early Romantic period. Early success in Germany, where he also revived interest in the music of Johann Sebastian Bach, was followed by travel throughout Europe. His essentially conservative musical tastes, however, set him apart from many of his more adventurous musical contemporaries such as Franz Liszt, Richard Wagner and Hector Berlioz. The Leipzig Conservatoire (now the University of Music and Theatre Leipzig), which he founded, became a bastion of this anti-radical outlook. His Violin Concerto was his last large orchestral work and is one of the most popular and most frequently performed violin concertos of all time. The concerto was first performed in Leipzig on 13 March 1845 with Ferdinand David as soloist. Mendelssohn was unable to conduct due to illness and the premiere was conducted by the Danish composer Niels Gade.
Franz Liszt

Franz Liszt became renowned in Europe during the nineteenth century for his virtuosic skill as a pianist. He was said by his contemporaries to have been the most technically advanced pianist of his age. In the 1840s he was considered by some to be perhaps the greatest pianist of all time. He was also a well-known composer, piano teacher, and conductor. He was a benefactor to other composers, including Richard Wagner, Hector Berlioz, Camille Saint-Saëns, Edvard Grieg and Alexander Borodin. He left behind an extensive and diverse body of work in which he influenced his forward-looking contemporaries and anticipated some 20th-century ideas and trends. When Liszt took up a long-standing invitation of Grand Duchess Maria Pavlovna of Russia to settle at Weimar, the most important period of his creative work began. Liszt had ample time to compose and during the next 12 years revised or produced those orchestral and choral pieces upon which his reputation as a composer mainly rested.
Schubert's 'Unfinished'

Franz Schubert's Symphony No. 8 in B minor, commonly known as the 'Unfinished Symphony' (German: Unvollendete), was started in 1822 but left with only two movements known to be complete, even though Schubert would live for another six years. After his death, the work fell into oblivion, until Johann von Herbeck found it in the possession of Schubert's friend Anselm Hüttenbrenner in 1865. Herbeck conducted the symphony in the same year, and the performance was met with great enthusiams by the audience. The work is often referred to as Schubert’s first romantic symphony owing to its emphasis on expressive melody, vivid harmony, and creative combinations of orchestral tone color.
Johann Strauss

Johann Strauss (son) was an Austrian composer of light music, particularly dance music and operettas. He composed over 500 waltzes, polkas, quadrilles, and other types of dance music, as well as several operettas and a ballet. In his lifetime, he was known as 'The Waltz King', and was largely then responsible for the popularity of the waltz in Vienna during the 19th century. Some of Johann Strauss's most famous works include The Blue Danube, Kaiser-Walzer, Tales from the Vienna Woods, the Tritsch-Tratsch-Polka, and the Pizzicato Polka. Among his operettas, Die Fledermaus and Der Zigeunerbaron are the most well-known. The operetta 'Die Fledermaus' premièred on 5 April 1874 at the Theater an der Wien in Vienna, and has been part of the regular operetta repertoire ever since.
Gustav Mahler

Gustav Mahler was a late-Romantic Austrian composer and one of the leading conductors of his generation. As a composer, he acted as a bridge between the 19th century Austro-German tradition and the modernism of the early 20th century. While in his lifetime his status as a conductor was established beyond question, his own music gained wide popularity only after periods of relative neglect which included a ban on its performance in much of Europe during the Nazi era. After graduating from the Vienna Conservatory in 1878, he held a succession of conducting posts of rising importance in the opera houses of Europe, culminating in his appointment in 1897 as director of the Vienna Court Opera (Hofoper). His innovative productions and insistence on the highest performance standards ensured his reputation as one of the greatest of opera conductors, particularly as an interpreter of the stage works of Wagner and Mozart.
Richard Strauss

Richard Georg Strauss was a leading German composer of the late Romantic and early modern eras. He is known for his operas, which include Der Rosenkavalier and Salome, his Lieder - especially his Four Last Songs - and his tone poems and other orchestral works, such as Death and Transfiguration, Till Eulenspiegel's Merry Pranks, Also sprach Zarathustra, An Alpine Symphony, and Metamorphosen. Strauss was also a prominent conductor throughout Germany and Austria. Strauss, along with Gustav Mahler, represents the late flowering of German Romanticism after Richard Wagner, in which pioneering subtleties of orchestration are combined with an advanced harmonic style. In 1905, Strauss produced Salome, a somewhat dissonant modernist opera based on the play by Oscar Wilde, in 1909 followd Elektra. Both were performed in Dresden for the first time.
Anton Bruckner

Anton Bruckner was an Austrian composer known for his symphonies, masses, and motets. The first are considered emblematic of the final stage of Austro-German Romanticism because of their rich harmonic language, strongly polyphonic character, and considerable length. Bruckner's compositions helped to define contemporary musical radicalism, owing to their dissonances, unprepared modulations, and roving harmonies. Unlike other musical radicals, such as Richard Wagner or Hugo Wolf who fit the enfant terrible mould, Bruckner showed extreme humility before other musicians, Wagner in particular. The apparent dichotomy between Bruckner the man and Bruckner the composer hampers efforts to describe his life in a way that gives a straightforward context for his music. His works, the symphonies in particular, had detractors, most notably the influential Austrian critic Eduard Hanslick, and other supporters of Johannes Brahms. He died in 1896.
Arnold Schönberg

Arnold Schönberg was an Austrian composer and painter, associated with the expressionist movement in German poetry and art, and leader of the Second Viennese School. In the 1920s, Schönberg developed the twelve-tone technique, a widely influential compositional method of manipulating an ordered series of all twelve notes in the chromatic scale. He also coined the term developing variation, and was the first modern composer to embrace ways of developing motifs without resorting to the dominance of a centralized melodic idea. Mondnacht

Joseph Freiherr von Eichendorff was a German poet and novelist of the later German romantic school. Eichendorff's guiding poetic theme was that Man should find happiness in full absorption of the beauties and changing moods of Nature. The lyricism of Eichendorff's poetry is much praised, and his poems have been set by many composers, including Schubert, Schumann, Mendelssohn, Brahms, Hugo Wolf, Richard Strauss, Friedrich Nietzsche, Hans Pfitzner, and Alexander Zemlinsky. In 1837, his poem 'Mondnacht' (Night of the Moon) was published, which is often seen as the 'pearl of pearls' of german romantic lyricism.
Carl Spitzweg

Carl Spitzweg was a German romanticist painter and poet. He is considered to be one of the most important artists of the Biedermeier era. His father, a wealthy merchant, had Carl trained as a pharmacist. He attained his qualification from the University of Munich, but while recovering from an illness he also took up painting. Spitzweg was self-taught as an artist, and began by copying the works of Flemish masters. He contributed his first work to satiric magazines. Upon receiving an inheritance in 1833, he was able to dedicate himself to painting. His later paintings and drawings were often humorous genre works. In 1839, his first painting 'The Poor Poet' was published.
Clemens Brentano

Clemens Brentano was a German poet and novelist, born in Ehrenbreitstein, near Koblenz. Brentano, whose early writings were published under the pseudonym Maria, belonged to the Heidelberg group of German romantic writers, and his works are marked by excess of fantastic imagery and by abrupt, bizarre modes of expression. On the whole his finest work is the collection of Romanzen vom Rosenkranz (published posthumously in 1852). His short stories were very popular. The latter part of his life he spent in Regensburg, Frankfurt and Munich, actively engaged in promoting the Catholic faith. Against his will, his works were often seen as devotional literature.
